gos_code.comment: Grey goshawk are part of the potential pool, however, they are definitely seen (by me, in flight) at Huon Ridge.

offpool.comment: I can confirm that all of these detections/IDs are real and confirmed by me!

rat_split.comment: That camera (hr_c15) was temporarily (experimentally) baited with a single pile of cooked chickpeas that lasted for a few weeks, and it was during this period that the swamp rats first showed up! This also led to a flurry of short-term activity at that camera, as the residue was consumed by various species. No other cameras at Huon Ridge were ever baited, before or after.

unk_code.comment: Data coding error, these should be standardised.

definition.purpose: The Huon Ridge pool is frozen and the development detections are open. Questions 1 to 4 settle what some codes and labelling practices mean, which determines how records map to the pool. Question 5 decides how the frozen pool treats native species that were detected but never entered it.

questions.context: It has two daytime records, at hr_c10 on 10 February 2020 and hr_c9 on 23 April 2020, and no entry in hr_taxa.csv. Both goshawks are primary-pool 'occasional' species that are otherwise never detected at either site.
questions.prompt: Which species is the code 'gos' in hr_obs.csv?

questions.context: 'unk' has 1,215 records at 27 cameras, all between May 2023 and July 2024. 'ukn', your usual unknown-animal code, has 6,111 records across the whole record.

options.label: A classifier 'unknown' that I did not resolve

questions.prompt: What does 'unk' mean in hr_obs.csv, as distinct from 'ukn'?

questions.context: The 2024-25 MEWC table carries an 'expert_updated' flag. If small-bird detection differs between your manual identifications and classifier-assisted ones, bird encounter rates would shift at the switch-over. That is the Huon Ridge version of the labelling question you answered for Judbury.

options.label: Every final label is my own identification; the classifier only pre-sorted
Classifier labels above a confidence threshold were accepted; I checked the rest
Something else; see comment, including when the classifier was introduced

questions.prompt: How were Huon Ridge identifications made once the MEWC classifier was in use?

questions.context: Swamp rat records begin in June 2022: 852 records at 4 cameras. Black rat has 1,466 records at 17 cameras from 2019 to 2024. Judbury's 12 rat records are all labelled black rat.

options.label: Yes; swamp rats simply first appeared in 2022
No; before mid-2022 swamp rats may have been labelled black rat

questions.prompt: Were swamp rats always distinguished from black rats at Huon Ridge?

questions.context: None of these had an ALA record within 10 km, so none entered the pool: swamp rat (852 records), painted button-quail (1) and an unidentified skink (1). Non-native brown hare, brown rat, cattle and chickens are also off-pool. Adding species after seeing detections makes the pool detection-informed. Claude recommends keeping the frozen primary pool and reporting results with and without the additions, as you chose for co3.

options.label: Keep the frozen primary pool; add a separate post-freeze additions stratum and report results with and without it
Keep the frozen pool unchanged; report off-pool detections only as a measured limit of ALA-based pool building
Add the swamp rat, and any other native ground species, to the primary pool as a documented amendment

questions.prompt: How should the frozen pool treat native species detected at Huon Ridge that never entered it?
